Hi and thank you for speaking up.

Think of it as the ability to vote in real life. To be able to vote in any modern country, you have to be, say, 18 years old. Why can't tourists from, say Russia, vote in USA, or why can't Americans just travel to Russia and vote on Russian elections?

At WhoaVerse, you are free to submit comments, links and start discussions but you can not influence other users or the system by instantly having the right to vote the moment you sign up for an account.

The reason we imposed voting restrictions on new accounts is because there are people out there (spammers, to name a few) who abused the "no limit voting" we initially had. By simply creating dozens of accounts they would be able to upvote anything to the frontpage (or downvote anything) and create a lot of noise.

By forcing people to write 20 comments (where each comment has to be upvoted at least once by the community), we are changing the game. It is not a perfect solution, but it works.

You are more than welcome to submit ideas on how we could improve this.
